newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds let U.S. call the tune.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds let U.S. call the tune.

text.p: *Australia bonds saw their slowest trading session for some weeks as the market wound down for the year-end holidays, while the rise in yields reflected an easier U.S. market.
Australia bonds succumbed to their slowest trading session for some weeks as the market wound down for the year-end holidays.
"I think a lot of people have closed up their books for the year, so I suspect we're not going to see much now until the new year," one trader said.
In the meantime, the U.S. Treasury market is likely to call the direction of the local market with no major domestic data due out until early January.
The market got off on a weak footing on a U.S.-led markdown, but this was pared in thin liquidity, traders said.
This partial recovery reflected an acute stock shortage in the benchmark 2006 bond, which also prompted a short squeeze during Wednesday's session, traders said.
However, concerns over potential interest in a US$12.5 billion five-year U.S. note auction following a disappointing result to yesterday's two-year note sale weighed on the market.
A flurry of U.S. indicators before final auction bids are due in are likely to set the tone for the note sale.
This data includes the latest weekly jobless claims, October international trade and December Philadelphia Fed survey.

Local bond yield spreads to the U.S. ended little changed, but remained tighter to Canadian debt following Wednesday's stronger than expected Canadian CPI. New Zealand bonds were more perkier as the market took heart to a rise in the N.Z. dollar and outpaced domestic bonds.
